research_question: What is the effect of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESA), compared with placebo or usual care, on acute kidney injury?
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates a lower incidence or risk of acute kidney injury in the erythropoiesis-stimulating agent group compared to control (favoring ESA).
search_queries: erythropoietin acute kidney injury randomized controlled trial
darbepoetin placebo acute kidney injury trial
inclusion_criteria: Controlled clinical trials evaluating erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (e.g., recombinant human erythropoietin, darbepoetin) compared with placebo or usual care
Studies conducted in human patient populations at risk of or evaluated for acute kidney injury
Reporting quantitative incidence or event counts of acute kidney injury
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent and a control condition (placebo, usual care, or no treatment)
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size for acute kidney injury (e.g., event counts, proportions, odds ratios, or risk ratios)
Non-human (in vitro or animal) studies or studies completely unrelated to the research question
moderators_to_extract: Patient population / clinical setting (e.g., cardiac surgery, ICU/critically ill, contrast-induced nephropathy, trauma)
Specific ESA type (e.g., epoetin alfa, epoetin beta, darbepoetin alfa)
Timing and route of ESA administration (e.g., intravenous vs. subcutaneous; pre-operative vs. peri-operative)
AKI diagnostic criteria / definition (e.g., KDIGO, AKIN, RIFLE, serum creatinine threshold)
Control arm type (placebo vs. usual care / no treatment)
effect_size_note: Trials reporting zero events in both arms are treated as not estimable and excluded from pooling.
